D1.text: Every user-visible error is exactly one `line N: <message>` line, no traceback

D2.text: Evaluator is iterative for calls/blocks: user nesting depth never becomes Python stack depth

D3.text: Integer division/remainder truncate toward zero for negative operands

D4.text: REPL uses the exact prompt string and exits cleanly on EOF (Ctrl-D)

Q1.text: Conditions (if/while, and/or operands) must be booleans; non-boolean is a runtime error

Q2.text: `let` declares a new binding, `set` reassigns an existing one; bare assignment is a parse error

Q3.text: String concatenation is `~`; `+` on strings is a type error

Q4.text: Not-equals is `<>`; `!=` is a lex error

Q6.text: Comparisons do not chain (a < b < c is a parse error)

Q7.text: `and`/`or` never short-circuit; both operands are always evaluated

SC1.text: Python standard library only; no third-party packages

SC10.text: Every CLI entry point dispatched from a single bract/__main__.py

SC11.text: Line numbers surfaced to users are 1-indexed

SC12.text: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub in modules reachable from __main__ once a feature is claimed complete

SC2.text: Single-package layout: every module directly under bract/

SC3.text: All errors rendered through one shared error-formatting path

SC4.text: No print()/stdout/stderr writes outside the CLI module

SC6.text: Exit codes are exactly {0,1,2}, produced only by the CLI dispatch

SC7.text: No Python eval/exec/compile anywhere in bract/

SC8.text: No module-level mutable interpreter state; state threaded through an Interpreter/Environment

SC9.text: bract fmt only changes whitespace/indentation/brace placement, never AST

hints: should I update DESIGN.md
can I fix a mistake in the design doc
spec seems wrong or contradictory
design doc correction
req-0985.statement: DESIGN.md is frozen as of the seed-v1 tag; never edit it to fix a mistake or add a correction. Later corrections to the implementation arrive only as task-prompt text.

hints: command to run the bract test suite
how to run tests locally before finishing a task
req-0c46.statement: Run the Bract test suite with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, and run it locally before declaring an implementation task done.

hints: negative number division result is wrong
why not just use Python's // operator
integer division rounding direction
mixed-sign division truncate vs floor
implementing the / and % builtins
req-0d8a.statement: Integer division truncates toward zero for mixed-sign operands, never floors.

hints: repl crashes on ctrl-d
handling EOF in the repl
repl exit code on stdin close
uncaught exception ending repl session
req-0e57.statement: On the REPL, EOF on stdin (Ctrl-D) must end the session cleanly with exit code 0, not raise an uncaught exception.

hints: comparing two strings with less than
ordering comparison on booleans or nil
why does < error on strings
lexicographic string comparison in bract
req-194e.statement: Ordering comparisons (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`) are Integer-only; applying one to strings, booleans, or nil is a runtime type error, never a lexicographic or truthiness-based comparison.

hints: should the README repeat the grammar
where should language semantics be documented
keeping README and DESIGN.md in sync
why does the README just link to DESIGN.md instead of explaining syntax
avoiding duplicated docs that can drift
req-2430.statement: README.md and other user-facing docs should point to DESIGN.md for grammar and semantics rather than restate them, so the two documents can't drift apart.

hints: implementing the != operator
bang equals token
why does the parser never see !=
req-251e.statement: Not-equals is spelled `<>`, not `!=`. There is no `!` token at all — a lexer that hits `!` raises a lex error ('unexpected character !'); `!=` is unreachable at the parser and must not be special-cased there.

hints: shortcut using python eval or exec
compiling bract to python bytecode
translating bract AST into python code
req-2775.statement: No Python `eval`, `exec`, or `compile` anywhere in `bract/`. The interpreter must be a genuine tree-walker over its own AST, not a translation layer onto Python's own evaluator.

hints: formatter changing program semantics
canonical formatter reordering expressions
does bract fmt preserve precedence
req-2ab6.statement: `bract fmt` only ever changes whitespace, indentation, and brace placement. It must never reorder, re-associate, or drop AST nodes — expression grouping, operator precedence, and evaluation order are exactly preserved.

hints: should bract fmt be idempotent
running fmt twice changes the file
formatter output not stable
fmt of fmt equality test
req-30fd.statement: `bract fmt` output must be byte-stable: running the formatter on its own output is a no-op (fmt composed with fmt equals fmt).

hints: off-by-one in at or sub
python slice equivalent for sub
indexing a string at position 0
substring end index inclusive or exclusive
req-3813.statement: String builtins (`at`, `len`, `sub`) are 1-indexed, not 0-indexed. `at(s, 0)` is out of range — not the first character. `sub(s, start, end)` is inclusive on both ends, unlike Python's exclusive-end slicing.

hints: repl prompt text
what does the bract prompt look like
repl output doesn't match expected transcript
req-3a2f.statement: The REPL prompt string is exactly `bract> ` (with a trailing space).

hints: concatenating strings with plus
string + string
using + between a string and an int
req-49ee.statement: String concatenation is `~`, never `+`. `+` is exclusively integer addition; applying it to any string operand (alone or with an int) is a type error ('+ cannot be applied to strings'), never silent coercion or concatenation.

hints: can I add a dependency
pip install a library
adding a requirements.txt or third-party import
req-4b1c.statement: Python standard library only: no third-party package is ever imported, pip-installed, or listed in any dependency file, anywhere in this project's implementation.

hints: python traceback leaking to the user
uncaught exception printed to stderr
multi-line error output
req-4d8f.statement: Every user-visible error (lex, parse, or runtime) is rendered as exactly one line, 'line N: <message>', from a single shared error-formatting path — no Python tracebacks, exception class names, ANSI color, or secondary lines.

hints: sub with start greater than end
reversed substring range
empty string vs error for sub bounds
what happens if start is bigger than end in sub
req-5604.statement: sub(s, start, end) returns the empty string when start > end, rather than raising an error.

hints: let inside a while loop raising already-declared error
closure not seeing outer variable after function returns
fresh scope per loop iteration
req-59c6.statement: Each `while` iteration and each function call starts with a fresh, empty innermost scope. A `let` inside a loop body declares anew every iteration rather than colliding with the previous iteration's binding. `fn` values are real closures — a returned inner `fn` still sees its outer `let` bindings after the outer call returns.

hints: adding bracket indexing syntax for strings
s[0] style access
array-like indexing in bract
req-5b07.statement: There is no subscript/index syntax (`s[0]`) anywhere in the grammar. String indexing exists exclusively through the `at`/`sub` builtins — do not add bracket parsing as a convenience.

hints: can user code redefine len or at
are builtins user-declared functions
where do string builtins come from
shadowing a builtin name
req-6e1c.statement: The string builtins (len, at, sub) are always available in the evaluator environment; they are not declared, imported, or overridable by user code.

hints: what exit code should the program return
process exit status for a runtime vs parse error
req-7310.statement: Exit codes are exactly 0 (success), 1 (runtime error), 2 (lex/parse error), produced only by `bract run` and top-level CLI dispatch. No other exit code is ever returned.

hints: bare assignment without let or set
redeclaring a variable in the same scope
mutating a captured closure variable
shadowing a variable in an inner scope
req-7b3e.statement: `let x = expr;` declares a new binding and errors if `x` is already declared in the *same* scope ('already declared'); shadowing an outer scope is fine. `set x = expr;` reassigns an existing binding found by walking outward and errors if none exists ('not declared'). Bare `x = expr;` without let/set is a parse error.

hints: why does fmt remove parentheses
formatted output missing parens from source
should the formatter preserve parentheses
does bract track grouping in the AST
round-trip changed my parenthesized expression
req-7c32.statement: The Bract grammar does not represent source parenthesization as its own AST node; operator precedence is captured purely by tree structure, so the formatter (and any other AST-to-source pass) cannot recover or reproduce parentheses from the original source.

hints: should this new module go in a subpackage
organizing bract modules into subfolders
req-836f.statement: Single-package layout: every interpreter module lives directly under `bract/` (e.g. `bract/lexer.py`). No nested subpackages like `bract/core/` or `bract/lexer/`.

hints: why is it called bract and not sprout
renaming the language
checking for language name collisions
req-8804.statement: The language is named 'Bract', not the earlier working name 'Sprout'. 'Sprout' was rejected because at least four existing languages use it, including a same-shaped Python tree-walking interpreter on PyPI.

hints: should this silently coerce types
why is mixing int and string an error instead of converting
implicit conversion between types
req-8f7d.statement: Bract has no implicit type conversion anywhere: every operator's operand types are fixed, and a type mismatch is always a runtime type error, never a silent coercion.

hints: deep recursion crashes the interpreter
Python RecursionError on nested bract calls
does the evaluator need to be iterative
stack overflow on deep function calls
explicit stack instead of Python recursion for eval
req-91cd.statement: The evaluator must be iterative for function calls and nested blocks: no recursion on user-controlled Bract nesting/call depth.

hints: why is bract run printing extra output
does bract run echo expression values
bract run vs repl output differences
unexpected output from running a bract file
req-a1bc.statement: `bract run FILE` must not implicitly print expression-statement results the way the REPL does; it should produce only whatever output the program itself writes, plus the one-line error format on failure.

hints: merge conflict during automated rebase
how to resolve conflicts in the cloche pipeline
should I abort or merge instead of rebase --continue
req-a2ee.statement: When the automated pipeline hits a merge conflict during rebase, resolve each conflicted file semantically (understand and integrate both sides, don't just pick one). Never run `rebase --abort`, never merge, and never delete a branch — report success and let the merge step perform the fast-forward itself.

hints: if(0) or if("") truthiness check
falsy value in a condition
why doesn't an empty string count as false
req-b564.statement: if/while conditions must evaluate to Boolean. There is no truthy/falsy coercion — 0, "", and nil are all type errors as conditions ('line N: condition must be a boolean'), not falsy values.

hints: using a global variable for bindings
module-level cache in the interpreter
singleton interpreter state across calls
req-b648.statement: No module-level mutable interpreter state (no global dict/list holding variable bindings, call stack, or program output across calls). All interpreter state is threaded explicitly through function arguments/return values or held on an explicit Interpreter/Environment instance.

hints: short-circuit evaluation of and/or
does the second operand of and always run
side effect in the right operand not happening
req-cc72.statement: `and`/`or` never short-circuit: both operands are always evaluated, in left-to-right order, regardless of the left operand's value — including any side effects in the right operand.

hints: chained comparison like a < b < c
python-style comparison chaining
parsing consecutive comparison operators
req-cf2f.statement: Comparison operators don't chain: the grammar accepts at most one comp-op per `comparison`. `a < b < c` must be a parse error ('comparisons do not chain'), never left-associated into `(a < b) < c` or treated as `a < b and b < c`.

hints: modulo negative numbers wrong sign
why is remainder negative
% operator gives unexpected sign
implementing the % builtin
division remainder invariant
req-d337.statement: Modulo (`%`) is derived from truncating division as `a - int(a/b)*b`, not Python's floor-based `%`, so the invariant `(a/b)*b + (a%b) == a` holds under truncation semantics.

hints: why doesn't format_error print anything
format_error returns a string instead of printing
error message never appeared on stderr
refactoring how errors get written to stderr
who is responsible for writing error output to a stream
req-de40.statement: format_error() in bract/errors.py is a pure formatting function that returns the formatted string; it must not write to stdout/stderr itself. Callers are responsible for writing the result to the correct stream, appending the trailing newline, and flushing.

hints: debugging with print statements in the lexer or parser
a module writing directly to stdout or stderr
req-dfc6.statement: No `print()`/`sys.stdout.write`/`sys.stderr.write` outside the CLI layer. Lexer, parser, and evaluator modules communicate exclusively through return values and raised exceptions.

hints: tests are failing what should I change
should I edit the test file to make a failing test pass
req-e716.statement: When the automated pipeline reports failing tests, fix the implementation to make them pass — never modify the test files themselves.

hints: how do I report task completion to cloche
run marked as failed despite finishing successfully
required final output format
req-f01a.statement: Every cloche task/step must end its output with exactly one CLOCHE_RESULT:success or CLOCHE_RESULT:fail marker as the final line of output. An agent that exits without printing the marker is treated as failed regardless of what the prose says.

hints: dividing by zero
modulo by zero
ZeroDivisionError leaking through
what error does division by zero raise
req-ffa8.statement: Division and remainder by zero raise the runtime error 'line N: division by zero' through the standard error path, for both `/` and `%`.
